label: Subtraction vocabulary: concrete presence, finitely many, could fail to exist, no newcomer
term: subtraction (concrete presence, possible failure to exist, subtraction without newcomer)
definition: On the route's profile m (frame m.ontic.frame, rigid candidates, world-relative existence m.ontic.ExistsAt, world-independent concreteness m.concrete): ConcretePresence m x v holds when x is concrete and exists at v. PossiblyFinitelyManyConcrete m w (A1): some world v accessible from w has all its concrete objects in one finite list. EachConcreteCouldFailAt m v (A2 at v): every concrete object existing at v is absent at some world accessible from v; ...Throughout m w asks this at every world accessible from w. NoNewcomer m v u: every concrete object existing at u exists at v. SubtractableAt m v (A3, conditional subtraction): every concrete object x existing at v that is absent at some world accessible from v is absent at some world u accessible from v with NoNewcomer m v u; NonNecessitationAt is the unconditional (literal) form, which equals A2 plus SubtractableAt. PossiblyNoConcrete m w: the stage-one JointAbsence of the concrete-presence predicate, some world accessible from w with no concrete object. NotEachConcreteCouldFailAt is the negation of A2 at w. Lowe's reply uses NecessaryAbstractumAt (a non-concrete candidate existing at every world accessible from w) and AbstractaNeedConcretaThroughout (at every accessible world, an existing non-concrete candidate requires some existing concrete object).
note: Analyst formulation, attribution deferred: Baldwin 1996, Rodriguez-Pereyra 1997 and 2002, Efird and Stoneham 2005 and Lowe 1998 and 2002 are navigation only, no source claim. Possibility is accessibility in the route's frame; nothing here asserts that the frame's worlds are the metaphysically possible worlds. 'Could fail to exist' is the frame's diamond of non-existence (the dual of the route's NecessaryAt, NECESSARY_2 box-existence), so A2 at w is with excluded middle exactly the denial of STMT-NECESSARY-CONCRETE-AT at w (controls). Finiteness is covering by a List because the family is zero-axiom and does not import Mathlib; covering by a finite list is the standard characterization of Set.Finite. A3 realizes the absence jointly at one world: pairwise absence (recombination) does not suffice (controls, pair model). Concreteness is the profile's parameter (INHABITED_CONCRETE_WORLD_2 usage); no causal or spatiotemporal criterion is built in.
